testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
Which merge-gating CI steps neither the Recipe's Test entrypoint nor its Check step runs could not be read (the snapshot agent reported nothing for it), so a passing run here is not known to cover them.

survived.claim: The ADR's Status line says decision 1 is amended by #4327, but decision 1's body is unchanged. It still says the Fit is 'computed at every phase 0' and that a run with no Fit routes 'by the starting table', which the amendment contradicts for a first run with no corpus.
survived.evidence: Line 3 reads: 'Amended by #4327: decision 1's Fit is computed at each phase 0 whose cost guard duty writes a guard; a phase 0 that writes no guard ... writes no Fit, and `route` beside no guard routes `slow-high` with no draw'. Line 15 still reads 'It is computed at every phase 0 ... A run whose Fit is missing or fails routes by the last Fit that computed, else by the starting table'. ticket-router.mjs:459 returns policy POLICY_CELL ('slow-high', ledger-grammar.mjs:855) with draw null when guard is null. The spec's decisions at lines 82 and 88 carry inline '*Amended (#4327)*' notes, but ADR decision 1 has none.
survived.suggested_fix: Add an inline '*Amended (#4327)*' note to decision 1 in the ADR, as the spec does. Alternatively, reword line 15 to say 'at each phase 0 whose guard duty writes a guard' and to say a no-guard run routes slow-high.

I only read the file; I ran no test or mutation, and a doc claim has none to run. In the snapshot's ADR 0037, line 3 (Status) says 'Amended by #4327: decision 1's Fit is computed at each phase 0 whose cost guard duty writes a guard; a phase 0 that writes no guard ... writes no Fit, and `route` beside no guard routes `slow-high` with no draw'. Line 15 (decision 1) still says 'computed at every phase 0' and 'else by the starting table', with no inline amendment note. refuted.claim: The new note says 'Only a phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records writes a guard and a Fit, and that Fit is the starting table's fit'. Read literally, this says a phase 0 whose corpus has counted records writes no guard and no Fit, which is false. The brief said 'Only a phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records writes a Fit that is the starting table's fit'; the PR moved 'a guard and' inside the scope of 'Only'.
refuted.evidence: Ran writeFit(cwd, {computed_at, verdict:'no_verdict', tripped:[], cells:[]}) from plugin/scripts/metrics-refresh.mjs (probe-fit.mjs). In the header-only corpus fixture: `n_rows 0 burn_in true`, `rows equal starting table rows? true`, cost row {"*":"slow-high"}, so this half of the note holds. In the copy's full corpus: `n_rows 268 burn_in true`, `rows equal starting table rows? false`, cost row {"*":"task-high"}, and .fleet/router-fit.json was written (4.6K). So a phase 0 with counted records also writes a Fit, beside the guard its cost guard duty wrote: metrics-refresh.mjs main() calls fit(repo, written) whenever costGuard returned a guard (lines 372-376, 386-404). Also: in a header-only corpus repo with no GitHub remote, `metrics-refresh.mjs --repo hdr` printed `cost guard failed: pr-cost.mjs --guard exited 2: pr-cost: gh pr list failed` and exited 1 with no Fit, so having a corpus alone is not enough to write a guard either.
refuted.suggested_fix: Use the brief's scoping: 'A phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records writes a guard and a Fit, and that Fit is the starting table's fit.' (drop 'Only'), or 'Only a phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records writes a Fit that is the starting table's fit.'

votes.reason: The sentence follows 'the Fit is computed at each phase 0 whose cost guard duty writes a guard', so in context it describes first-run cases. The claim's own probe confirms the stated case: with a header-only corpus the Fit equals the starting table. The literal reading that counted-records runs write no Fit contradicts the preceding clause, so it is a wording quibble, not a factual error. I read the doc line only and ran no code. The note is in an amendment about first runs. It contrasts a first run with no corpus (no guard, no Fit) against a phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records (guard and Fit, where the Fit is the starting table's). In that frame, 'Only' scopes the first-run cases. It does not say a phase 0 with counted records writes no Fit. The sentence is loosely worded, but I could not show it is a defect that needs fixing, so I default to refuted. I read line 88 of the spec and ran nothing, so I did not reproduce the claim's probe results or test the guard-failure case. CWD-AUDIT: not run (no files written in /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin).

It also says the no-guard routing twice in one sentence: 'routes `slow-high` with no draw because there is no guard' and then '(`route` beside no guard routes the default cell, whatever the table)'.
unverified.evidence: `grep -n -o 'each phase 0 whose cost guard duty writes a guard' docs/specs/2026-11-01-self-refining-router-design.md` → lines 17, 83, 88: the same clause three times within 72 lines, all added by this PR. In plugin/scripts/ticket-router.mjs, lines 447-448 ('the default cell when there is no guard'), 455 ('`draw` is null with no guard') and 620 ('With no guard the default cell is the only one') show that 'slow-high with no draw' and the parenthetical describe the same branch. Dropping either keeps the meaning.
unverified.suggested_fix: Line 88: `*Amended (#4327): a first run with no corpus writes no guard and so no Fit (see When), and routes `slow-high` with no draw whatever the table, not by a starting-table Fit. Only a phase 0 with a corpus but no counted records writes a guard and a Fit, and that Fit is the starting table's fit.*` This drops the third copy of the condition and the parenthetical that repeats the clause before it.

The phrase adds a reference the reader has to resolve, and the clause after it carries the whole meaning alone.
